newsitem.title: ITALY: Confidence vote seen likely for Italy mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Confidence vote seen likely for Italy mini-budget.

text.p: The Italian government will probably have to call a confidence vote in the Senate (upper house) to push its recent mini-budget past a swathe of opposition amendments and into law, the leader of the Senate budget committee said.
The package has already been approved in the lower house of parliament thanks to a do-or-die confidence vote, and most be approved by the Senate before May 28, or else be scrapped.
Parliamentary party leaders decided on Thursday that the final Senate vote should be held on May 22.
"At this point I think (the mini-budget) will probably go to a confidence vote," the budget committee's Romualdo Coviello told reporters.
"The Northern League party is continuing its sterile obstructionism, sticking to its 400 amendments, making it very hard to vote on the whole package in a single day," he said.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition has called 21 confidence votes during its year in office, mainly to side-step opposition filibustering, and is holding a 22nd such vote later on Thursday to ram a decree on Albanian refugees into law.
